title.en: Explain cheques issued but not presented

say.en: You give a supplier a cheque on 30 March. You write it in your cash book at once, but your bank pays it only when the supplier presents it, maybe in April. In this lesson: Explain cheques issued but not presented.
Explain cheques deposited but not cleared.

body.en: When a cheque is *issued*, the firm credits the bank column at once, but the bank debits the account only when the payee presents the cheque. Until then the pass book balance is higher than the cash book balance.
body.kn: ಚೆಕ್ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ತಕ್ಷಣ ನಗದು ಪುಸ್ತಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕ್ ಶಿಲ್ಕು ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದರೆ ಪಾಸ್ ಪುಸ್ತಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಅದನ್ನು ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿದಾಗ ಮಾತ್ರ. ಅಲ್ಲಿಯವರೆಗೆ ಪಾಸ್ ಪುಸ್ತಕದ ಶಿಲ್ಕು ಹೆಚ್ಚು.

title.en: On the board: Why timing creates a difference

say.en: A cheque issued is credited in our cash book at once.
The bank debits our account only when the payee presents it. Until then the pass book is higher.
A cheque deposited is debited in our cash book at once but credited by the bank only after collection.
Nayak Traders: 5,000 of cheques not yet presented, 4,000 not yet credited.

problem.en: Cash book of Nayak Traders shows ₹30,000 on 31 March. Cheques issued ₹12,000, of which ₹7,000 were presented by 31 March. Cheques deposited ₹10,000, of which ₹6,000 were credited by 31 March. Find the pass book balance.

steps.en: Cheques issued but not presented = 12,000 − 7,000 = ₹5,000 → add (PB higher).
Cheques deposited but not cleared = 10,000 − 6,000 = ₹4,000 → deduct (PB lower).

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. Cash book of Nayak Traders shows ₹30,000 on 31 March. Cheques issued ₹12,000, of which ₹7,000 were presented by 31 March. Cheques deposited ₹10,000, of which ₹6,000 were credited by 31 March. Find the pass book balance.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. Cash book of Nayak Traders shows 30,000 rupees on 31 March. Cheques issued 12,000, rupees of which 7,000 rupees were presented by 31 March. Cheques deposited 10,000, rupees of which 6,000 rupees were credited by 31 March. Find the pass book balance.
Cheques issued but not presented equals 12,000 minus 7,000 equals 5,000 rupees gives add PB higher.
Cheques deposited but not cleared equals 10,000 minus 6,000 equals 4,000 rupees gives deduct PB lower.
Pass book balance equals 30,000 plus 5,000 minus 4,000 equals 31,000 rupees.
So the answer is 31,000 rupees.

body.en: For every item ask: who has already recorded it, me or the bank? Then ask whether that entry raised or lowered the balance. The side that has recorded it has moved; the other side has not yet.
